We reviewed your July bill and the account records you provided. The July bill shows 880 kWh billed and the amount matches the meter register difference used for billing. At this stage we are not issuing a refund automatically; a human review is required before any credit can be made.

What we reviewed
We reviewed the June and July billing records, the three meter register reads on 2026-05-31 (actual), 2026-06-30 (estimated), and 2026-07-31 (actual), the most recent remote diagnostic from 2026-07-30, the published rate components, and the recent monthly usage history provided in your account records.

What we found
The July billed usage (880 kWh) equals the difference between the July 31, 2026 actual register reading and the prior register value used for billing (41380 - 40500 = 880 kWh). The June month-end read used for billing was an estimated value (40500) while July’s month-end read was an actual register read (41380). A remote diagnostic on 2026-07-30 returned PASS with no tamper or register-fault flags, and we have no recorded meter events in the supplied records.

Why your bill changed
Compared with June’s billed 500 kWh, July shows a 380 kWh increase. That increase is consistent with the register-read difference between the June value that was estimated and the July actual read. Because June’s month-end read was an estimate, the July actual read can appear higher if the estimate understated usage; we cannot tell from the supplied records whether the increase was due to actual higher usage or a correction after an under-estimate.

What happens next
We will request interval (smart meter) consumption data for May–July 2026 and ask you for a short statement about any changes in occupancy, appliance use, travel, or other events in July that could explain higher usage. If those items do not explain the spike, we will escalate the case for a human-reviewed meter inspection. Any refund or bill credit can only be made if the investigation documents a supported billing error or approved exception and then is approved by a Human Billing Supervisor.

What we need from you
Please provide a brief statement about July 2026 usage: any changes in household occupancy, appliance use, travel, or other events that could have increased consumption. If you have interval or smart-meter export data you can share, please provide that as well. We will proceed with data requests and update you after human review.

We reviewed your July bill and the account records you provided. The July bill shows 880 kWh billed and the amount matches the meter register difference used for billing. At this stage we are not issuing a refund automatically; a human review is required before any credit can be made.

What we reviewed
We reviewed the June and July billing records, the three meter register reads on 2026-05-31 (actual), 2026-06-30 (estimated), and 2026-07-31 (actual), the most recent remote diagnostic from 2026-07-30, the published rate components, and the recent monthly usage history provided in your account records.

What we found
The July billed usage (880 kWh) equals the difference between the July 31, 2026 actual register reading and the prior register value used for billing (41380 - 40500 = 880 kWh). The June month-end read used for billing was an estimated value (40500) while July’s month-end read was an actual register read (41380). A remote diagnostic on 2026-07-30 returned PASS with no tamper or register-fault flags, and we have no recorded meter events in the supplied records.

Why your bill changed
Compared with June’s billed 500 kWh, July shows a 380 kWh increase. That increase is consistent with the register-read difference between the June value that was estimated and the July actual read. Because June’s month-end read was an estimate, the July actual read can appear higher if the estimate understated usage; we cannot tell from the supplied records whether the increase was due to actual higher usage or a correction after an under-estimate.

What happens next
We will request interval (smart meter) consumption data for May–July 2026 and ask you for a short statement about any changes in occupancy, appliance use, travel, or other events in July that could explain higher usage. If those items do not explain the spike, we will escalate the case for a human-reviewed meter inspection. Any refund or bill credit can only be made if the investigation documents a supported billing error or approved exception and then is approved by a Human Billing Supervisor.

What we need from you
Please provide a brief statement about July 2026 usage: any changes in household occupancy, appliance use, travel, or other events that could have increased consumption. If you have interval or smart-meter export data you can share, please provide that as well. We will proceed with data requests and update you after human review.
